SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Harper Demo is a 42-year-old female presenting with low back pain.
She reports onset of low back pain on 06/13/2026.
Pain is located in the lumbar region, radiates to the buttocks, aggravated by prolonged sitting and bending, relieved by lying down.
She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bowel or bladder dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.
On examination, she has tenderness over the paraspinal muscles L3-L5, limited forward flexion due to pain.
Examination reveals radiculopathy with diminished ankle reflex and L5/S1 weakness.
Assessment: Lumbar radiculopathy, likely L5/S1.
Plan: Initiate NSAIDs, start physical therapy, and follow up in 2 weeks.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Harper Demo returns for follow-up after initiating NSAIDs and physical therapy.
NSAIDs were started on 06/14/2026 and continued through 07/25/2026 with partial relief.
Physical therapy was initiated on 06/20/2026 for a total of 10 sessions and concluded on 07/25/2026 without improvement.
She continues to report low back pain with intermittent radicular symptoms.
Examination shows mild tenderness lumbar paraspinals, unchanged neurologic findings.
Assessment: Persistent lumbar radiculopathy with partial response to NSAIDs and no improvement with PT.
Plan: Continue NSAIDs as needed, consider alternative medications, and obtain lumbar MRI if symptoms persist.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Harper Demo presents for routine follow-up.
She reports ongoing low back pain with radiculopathy.
Review of treatment: NSAIDs were started on 06/14/2026 and continued through 07/25/2026 with partial relief.
Physical therapy was initiated on 06/20/2026 for a total of 10 sessions and concluded on 07/25/2026 without improvement.
Plan: Obtain lumbar MRI to further evaluate anatomic correlates; if MRI shows significant pathology, spine surgery referral will be considered.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Harper Demo returns after follow-up; lumbar MRI ordered today.
Pending lumbar MRI results, a spine surgery referral is under consideration.
She remains symptomatic despite prior conservative measures.
Assessment: Persistent lumbar radiculopathy.
Plan: Await MRI results, then discuss surgical referral.
